status.main_product: Invoice and supply chain financing platform
status.scope_reason: The company operates a blockchain-based platform that provides digital invoice factoring and supply chain finance solutions.
status.evidence: According to Tracxn and corporate records, Volo Fin Pte. Ltd. is currently an active entity incorporated in Singapore.

claims.claim: The company reports that its blockchain-based digital platform facilitates automated supplier self-onboarding, real-time in-principle approval, buyer risk assumption, and digital portal visibility for managing credit limits up to $10 million.

The company reports utilizing an API integration on its platform to automatically screen onboarded individuals and parent entities for potential matches against money laundering and sanctions blacklists.
claims.source: Panel 4 Discussion on Digital KYC and AML Interview with Roshan Shah

claims.claim: In November 2022, VoloFin completed and disbursed its first set of cross-border export financing transactions on Vayana TradeXchange (VTX), an international trade financing services platform operating under the IFSCA.
claims.source: PR Newswire and Livemint reports on Vayana TradeXchange operations

claims.claim: VoloFin Corp reports that its digital supply chain and invoice factoring platform is a next-generation IT platform built on blockchain fabric with integrated artificial intelligence capabilities to automate customer onboarding, KYC, credit checks, and digitized workflows.
claims.source: VoloFin USA Official Website (volofinusa.com) and Crunchbase Company Profile

claims.claim: In an executive interview, the company reported that it has shifted its core platform development entirely in-house to transition toward its "Version 3" launch and integrated multiple external APIs to enhance due diligence data streaming.
claims.source: Fintech Watch Exclusive Interview with Roshan Shah

claims.claim: In 2021, the company announced the launch of its blockchain-powered invoice financing platform designed to automate onboarding, KYC compliance, and transaction tracking.
claims.source: Reuters article (March 23, 2021) and VoloFin corporate website

claims.claim: The company reports anonymized case studies from small and medium-sized enterprise clients who started working with the platform in 2021, including an engineering goods exporter, a chillies exporter from Guntur, and a garment exporter from New Delhi.
claims.source: VoloFin corporate website case studies section

claims.claim: VoloFin announced a strategic partnership in March 2022 with US-based alternative asset management group Highmore to extend trade finance and invoice financing solutions to small and medium-sized enterprises.
claims.source: Global Trade Review and VoloFin official press release (March 17, 2022)

claims.claim: The company reports that its global trade finance network spans over 50 countries.
claims.source: VoloFin official LinkedIn profile and corporate overview

claims.claim: The company reports securing a $50 million funding line structured via a notes programme from an unnamed top-five US-based global bank in November 2024 to expand its trade finance services for Indian exporters.
claims.source: Business Standard and YourStory media coverage (November 18, 2024)

claims.claim: The company reports a strategic partnership established in January 2022 with Highmore's Trade and Specialty Finance business to deliver joint working capital solutions.
claims.corrected: The company reports a strategic partnership established in March 2022 with Highmore's Trade and Specialty Finance business to deliver joint working capital solutions.

claims.claim: The company reports that it has factored over $125 million in invoices since its inception in 2020.
The company reports securing a $50 million funding facility from a major United States bank in November 2024 to support 250 to 350 export businesses.
